title: FedREST-HIDS: split-federated intrusion detection for resource-heterogeneous Industrial IoT
description:
Reference implementation and experimental notebooks accompanying the article "FedREST-HIDS: Split-Federated Intrusion Detection for Resource-Heterogeneous Industrial IoT" (Vyas, Hwang & Lin), submitted to Computer Communications.

FedREST-HIDS partitions intrusion detection across three tiers. Resource-rich devices train complete local models and take part in federated learning. Resource-constrained devices execute only the initial feature-extraction layer and transmit clipped, noised activations to an edge server that runs the remaining layers. Federated transfer learning then aligns the edge models globally, and a trust-aware aggregation rule (FedTrust) bounds the influence of any single client. Privacy is enforced locally under Rényi differential privacy.

Contents

  • src/fedrest/ — reference implementation: Rényi DP accounting, FedTrust aggregation, split models, communication cost model, training loops
  • notebooks/ — the notebooks that produced the reported results, preserved as run, with a manifest mapping each to the tables and figures it supports
  • scripts/verify_against_paper.py — 24 assertions checking the implementation against every privacy and communication figure printed in the article; runs in a second with no dataset and no GPU
  • scripts/audit_configs.py — prints each notebook's declared privacy configuration beside the article's reported settings
  • scripts/make_figure2.py — regenerates Figure 2 from the verification run's per-round log
  • results/ — output of the WUSTL-IIoT-2021 verification run
  • docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md — documents, in public, where the code and the article agree and where they diverge

Datasets are not redistributed. WUSTL-IIoT-2021, ToN-IoT and SCVIC-APT-2021 must be obtained from their original sources; see the README.
